title: Камера в кабинете  (The Camera in the Office)

segments.t: With Katya refusing to answer his phone calls, desperate Denis approaches Vika once more to ask her to speak with Katya. When Senya overhears them talking about what supposedly happened in the office, Vika suddenly remembers that a hidden camera records her office twenty-four hours a day. Let's listen to their discovery in Russian.
Вика, мне очень нужна твоя помощь.
Я же сказала, решай проблемы сам.
Катя совсем не хочет меня видеть.
Она даже на звонки не отвечает.
Может, ты сама с ней поговоришь?
Да, мне она, конечно, сразу поверит!
Скажи ей, что ничего не было.
Простите, я тут ничего не слышал.
Подожди, об этом уже все знают?
Ладно, пойдём скорее со мной.
В кабинете камера пишет всё круглосуточно.
Ты сможешь показать Кате эту запись.
Now let's break down how Vika finds a way to clear both their names line by line.
Вика, мне очень нужна твоя помощь.
'Vika, I really need your help.' A feminine short adjective of need agrees with the nominative subject phrase meaning your help.
Я же сказала, решай проблемы сам.
'I already told you, solve your problems yourself.' Vika reminds him of her earlier refusal using a singular imperfective imperative.
Катя совсем не хочет меня видеть.
'Katya does not want to see me at all.' Denis explains that Katya is avoiding him, using a negated verb and infinitive.
Она даже на звонки не отвечает.
'She does not even answer phone calls.' The verb meaning to answer takes the directional preposition with the accusative plural of calls.
Может, ты сама с ней поговоришь?
'Maybe you will talk with her yourself?' He suggests that Katya might listen if Vika speaks to her woman to woman.
Да, мне она, конечно, сразу поверит!
'Yes, she will certainly believe me right away!' Vika points out sarcastically that a jealous girlfriend will hardly believe her supposed rival.
Скажи ей, что ничего не было.
'Tell her that nothing happened.' Just as Senya walks past, Denis blurts out the sensitive details of the rumor.
Простите, я тут ничего не слышал.
'Excuse me, I did not hear anything here.' Eyes wide with gossip, Senya backs out of the room with a polite plural apology.
Подожди, об этом уже все знают?
'Wait, does everyone know about this already?' Realizing that her own reputation in the restaurant is now at stake, Vika changes her mind.
Ладно, пойдём скорее со мной.
'All right, come along with me quickly.' She beckons Denis to follow her using an inclusive plural imperative of motion.
В кабинете камера пишет всё круглосуточно.
'The camera in the office records everything around the clock.' The adverb meaning twenty-four hours a day modifies the third-person singular verb records.
Ты сможешь показать Кате эту запись.

'You will be able to show Katya that recording.' A second-person singular perfective future modal verb governs an infinitive and dative noun. Let's hear the conversation between Denis, Vika, and Senya from start to finish.

Relieved that the office security camera recorded the entire incident, Denis follows Vika to download the video proof for Katya. Listen for the nouns meaning help, calls, and camera. See you in the next scene.
